relevance_note: Single-patient case report of Blau syndrome with a NOD2 variant: "genetic testing for mutations in the NOD2 gene, which revealed a heterozygous p. Arg334Trp (R334W) mutation in exon four, confirming BS/EOS".
method_note: Read the full text by hand; no tables in the paper; output assembled with a short Python script and every span checked verbatim against the Markdown. In scope: the single patient (label 'patient') and both parents, who were tested and found negative ('The parents of the patient' with no sex given, hence 'parent of patient' and 'parent of patient 2'); parents get no variant rows. Inheritance recorded as de novo because the paper states both parents were tested for the same mutation and 'The mutation was absent in either of the parents.' (wording read as absent in both); the term 'de novo' is not used. The variant is printed only as protein ('p. Arg334Trp (R334W)', exon four); no cDNA or transcript. Variant class and pathogenicity class are not stated (only 'mutation ... confirming BS/EOS'), so left not reported. Uveitis is recorded as observed from the authors' attribution 'Based on the triad of dermatitis, polyarthritis, and uveitis' together with posterior synechiae; the paper never uses the word uveitis in the ophthalmologic findings. Normal findings converted to excluded abnormalities under D-27: blood pressure (systemic hypertension), heart rate, temperature 36.5 at examination (fever; checklist fever marked excluded on this single normal temperature, which is an uncertain call), growth, laboratory panel, EMG and muscle biopsy, skin biopsy granulomas. 'Echocardiography and abdominal ultrasound findings were unremarkable' and normal renal function tests were recorded only as the investigations named; they were not used to exclude pericarditis, hepatomegaly, splenomegaly or the composite 'granulomatous nephritis or renal failure' checklist items. Normal ferritin, electrolytes, lipid profile, total protein, thyroid function, albumin and hepatitis serology were not given separate rows. Parents' 'did not show any signs of the disease' recorded as one excluded feature row each ('signs of the disease'); their checklist items stay not reported because the statement names no specific feature. Age at last evaluation taken as 4 years (admission age); age at diagnosis of Blau syndrome is not stated explicitly. Vital status not explicitly stated (left not reported). The paper says this is the second case reported in the region and cites ref 6 (Iriqat 2021) for a different patient; it does not state that this patient was described before. Minor timeline wording: rash at age 1, then 'Over the following 2 years' no rash, then joint symptoms 'at the age of 3'; not treated as a contradiction.
